Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 81, verses 1–10:

Makkiyya (Meccan), and it has twenty-nine verses, one hundred and four words, and five hundred and thirty letters.

Al-Shaykh al-Imam Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Sahl al-Masarkhi narrated to us by dictation, saying: Abu al-Wafa al-Mu'ammil ibn Isa al-Masarkhi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Qass narrated to us, saying: I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd al-Sana'i say:

I heard Ibn Umar say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever would like to look at the Day of Judgement, let him recite: ﴿When the sun is wound up﴾" [96] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/27; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/226.]].

And Sa'id ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Mutar informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Shurayk narrated to us, saying:

Ahmad ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Salam ibn Sulaym narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir narrated to us from Zayd, from Muslim, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites ﴿When the sun is wound up﴾, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, will protect him from being disgraced when his record is spread open" [97] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/273.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿When the sun is wound up﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn Abbas: it grows dark. Atiyya from him: it departs. Mujahid: it is annihilated. Qatada: its light is gone. Sa'id ibn Jubayr: it is wrapped up (ʿuwwirat), and in Persian kawirikard. Abu Salih: it is turned upside down; and from him also: it is cast down. It is said: "He struck him and kawwarahu," meaning he threw him down. Rabi' ibn Haytham: it is hurled. The basic meaning of takawwur in the speech of the Arabs is gathering one part of a thing onto another, like the winding of a turban (taklwir al-ʿimama), which is wrapping it around the head, and the winding of a bundle (kārah) of plants, which is gathering some of it onto the rest and wrapping it. So the meaning of His words ﴿When the sun is wound up﴾ is: its parts are gathered one onto another, then it is wrapped and thrown, and when this is done to it, its light departs. Its proof and parallel is His words, glorified is He: ﴿And the sun and the moon are joined together﴾ [[Surat al-Qiyama: 9.]].

﴿And when the stars fall, scattering﴾, meaning: they scatter from the sky and fall to the earth. It is said: "inkadara al-tair" means the bird fell from its nest.

Al-Ajjaj said:
"He saw the ḍarbān (a wild beast) in the open and swooped (fa-inkadar)."
[[That is, fa-inṣabb (swooped down); it is in Lisan al-Arab: 4/518.]]

And "inkadara al-qawm" means the people came in successive groups until they swooped down upon them. Dhu al-Rumma said:
"So his wild flank turned aside, and they swooped down, / pursuing without slackening, the hunter and the hunted."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 1/560.]]

Ibn Abbas: it changed.

﴿And when the mountains are set in motion﴾, from the surface of the earth, so they become scattered dust. ﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾: al-ʿishar are the pregnant she-camels in whom ten months of pregnancy have passed; the singular is ʿushara, and this remains their name until they give birth at the completion of a year, and they are at their most precious and valued to their people. ʿUṭṭilat means: left free and neglected; their owners abandoned them, and they were [....] [[Illegible in the manuscript.]] for their tails, so they were not ridden nor milked, and there was no property in the world more beloved to them than these, but they were occupied with other things that distracted them from them.

﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾.

Abd al-Khaliq informed us, saying: Ibn Habib informed us, saying: Abu al-Abbas al-Barti narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us from his father, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾, who said: Their gathering is their death. Ibn Abbas also said: the gathering of everything is death, except the jinn and mankind, for they will be made to stand at the Day of Resurrection. Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾ means: they were mixed together. Qatada: they were assembled. It was also said: they were resurrected so that Allah may judge between them.

﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. The people of Makka and Basra recited it with light emphasis (sukkirat), and others with the doubled letter (sayyirat). They differed about its meaning. Ibn Zayd, Shamir ibn Atiyya, Sufyan and Wahb said: they were kindled and became fire.

Ibn Abbas said: Allah will wrap the sun, the moon and the stars in the sea, then He will send upon it a westerly wind which will blow on it until it becomes fire.

Mujahid, Muqatil and al-Dahhak said: it means that some of them will be burst into one another, so the sweet and the salt, and all the seas, become one sea.

Al-Halabi said: they were filled. Rabi' ibn Haytham: they overflowed. Al-Hasan: they dried up. Qatada: their water departed, so not a drop remained in them. Qutayb: their waters became one sea, which is the scalding water for the people of the Fire.

Aqil informed us that Abu al-Faraj informed them from Ibn Jarir, who said: al-Hasan ibn al-Huraith narrated to us, saying: al-Fadl Musa narrated to us from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliya, who said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b told me: There are six signs before the Day of Resurrection: while people are in their markets, the light of the sun departs; while they are in that state, the stars scatter; while they are in that state, the mountains fall upon the surface of the earth, so they are made smooth, shake, and burn; the jinn flee to mankind and mankind to the jinn; beasts, birds and wild animals are mixed together, and some of them surge over others. That is His words, glorified is He: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. He said: they were mixed. ﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾, he said: He neglected them. ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾, he said: the jinn said to mankind: "We will bring you the news; go to the sea," and behold, it is fire blazing. He said: while they are in that state, the earth splits open in one crack, down to the seventh earth and up to the highest seventh heaven. He said: while they are in that state, a wind comes upon them and causes them to die.

﴿And when the souls are paired﴾.

Al-Hasan informed us, saying: al-Sanni informed us, saying: Abu Ya'la informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakkar narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Abi Nur narrated to us from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, concerning ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: [the companions] — every man with every people who used to do his deeds."[98] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/88.]]

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Khalid al-Wahbi narrated to us, saying: Isma'il narrated to us from Simak ibn Harb, that he heard al-Nu'man ibn Bashir say: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾ means: the wicked with the wicked, and the righteous with the righteous. Ibn Abbas said: this is until people become "three classes" (azwaj thalatha). Al-Hasan and Qatada said: each person is joined to his group, Jews with Jews and Christians with Christians. Rabi' ibn Khaytham: a person will be gathered with the companion of his deeds. Muqatil: the souls of the believers are paired with the dark-eyed houris (al-hur al-ʿin), and the souls of the disbelievers with the devils. Its parallel is His words: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾ [[Surat al-Saffat: 22.]]. It was also said: souls are paired with their deeds.

Muhammad ibn Hamdun informed us, saying: Makki informed us, saying: Hamad ibn al-Azhar narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us from his father, from Ikrima, concerning His words, glorified is He: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: the spirits are paired with the bodies.

﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾: the female infant who was killed and buried alive. She was named so because earth is thrown upon her, so it burdens her (yuʾudduhā), that is, weighs her down until she dies. They said: a man of the Arabs, when a daughter was born to him, if he wished to keep her, he would dress her in a garment of wool or hair, and she would herd the camels and sheep in the desert; and if he wished to kill her, he would leave her until she reached six years of age. Then her father would say to her mother: "Perfume her and adorn her, so I may take her to her in-laws," and he had dug a pit for her in the desert. When he brought her to the pit, he would say to her: "Look at this pit," and push her from behind into it, and he would not cast dirt over her head until the pit was level with the ground. This is His words, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿Shall he keep it in humiliation, or bury it in the dust?﴾ [[Surat al-Nahl: 59.]]. Ibn Abbas said: in the Jahiliyya, when a woman became pregnant and the time of her delivery came, she would dig a pit and give birth at the edge of the pit. If she bore a girl, she threw her into the pit; and if she bore a boy, she kept him. Some tribes of the Arabs did this, and about it one of them said:

"I named her, when she was born, 'she will die' / and the grave is a bound in-law I have thrown in."
[[al-Sihah: 1/249.]]

Qatada said: the people of Jahiliyya would kill one of their daughters and feed their dog; Allah reproached them for that and threatened them.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan narrated to us that: al-Furati narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mahdi al-Abbali and Yahya ibn Musa narrated to us, both saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Isra'il ibn Yunus informed us from Simak ibn Harb, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, say concerning the words of Allah, glorified is He:

﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾: Qays ibn Asim al-Tamimi came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I buried eight daughters in the Jahiliyya." He said: "Free a slave for each one of them." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a owner of camels." He said: "Then sacrifice a camel for each of them, if you wish" [99] [[Kanz al-Ummal: 2/546.]].

﴿Asked for what sin she was killed﴾. The common reading is in the passive form in both verbs, and it has two aspects. One: she is asked, and it is said to her: "For what sin were you killed?" and "For what immorality were you killed?" as one says: "Abd Allah said: he is going," and "I am going"; and "Abd Allah said: for what sin was he struck?" and "for what sin was he struck?" Both are permissible and valid. The other: she is asked about by those who buried her, as if you had said: they were asked, and it was said: "Where are your children, and for what sin did you kill them?"

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Muqri informed us, saying: al-Baghawi informed us in Baghdad, saying: Ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us, saying: Ziyad ibn Ayyub Daluyah narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us from a man whom they mention as Harun. Ziyad said: I did not hear it from him myself; from Hashim, from Jabir ibn Zayd, that he used to recite: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked for what sin she was killed﴾; and similarly recited Abu al-Duha and Muslim ibn Subayh.

﴿And when the pages are spread open﴾. The people of Madina, Syria and Basra, except Abu Amr, recited it with light emphasis, and others with the doubled letter, in accordance with His words: ﴿Pages spread open﴾ [[Surat al-Muddathir: 52.]].

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Harun narrated to us, saying: al-Yasiri narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us from Abd al-Hamid ibn Sulayman, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Musa narrated to us from Ata' ibn Bashshar, from Umm Salama, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection naked and barefoot." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about the women?" He said: "People will be occupied, O Umm Salama." She said: "And what will occupy them?" He said: "The spreading of the pages, in which are the weights of atoms and the weights of mustard seeds" [100] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/234.]].

﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾.

He said: while they are in that state, a wind comes upon them and causes them to die.

Ibn Abbas said: Allah will wrap the sun, the moon and the stars in the sea, then He will send upon it a westerly wind which will blow on it until it becomes fire.

Mujahid, Muqatil and al-Dahhak said: it means that some of them will be burst into one another, so the sweet and the salt, and all the seas, become one sea.

Al-Halabi said: they were filled. Rabi' ibn Haytham: they overflowed. Al-Hasan: they dried up. Qatada: their water departed, so not a drop remained in them. Qutayb: their waters became one sea, which is the scalding water for the people of the Fire.

Aqil informed us that Abu al-Faraj informed them from Ibn Jarir, who said: al-Hasan ibn al-Huraith narrated to us, saying: al-Fadl Musa narrated to us from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliya, who said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b told me: There are six signs before the Day of Resurrection: while people are in their markets, the light of the sun departs; while they are in that state, the stars scatter; while they are in that state, the mountains fall upon the surface of the earth, so they are made smooth, shake, and burn; the jinn flee to mankind and mankind to the jinn; beasts, birds and wild animals are mixed together, and some of them surge over others. That is His words, glorified is He: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. He said: they were mixed. ﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾, he said: He neglected them. ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾, he said: the jinn said to mankind: "We will bring you the news; go to the sea," and behold, it is fire blazing. He said: while they are in that state, the earth splits open in one crack, down to the seventh earth and up to the highest seventh heaven. He said: while they are in that state, a wind comes upon them and causes them to die.

﴿And when the souls are paired﴾.

Al-Hasan informed us, saying: al-Sanni informed us, saying: Abu Ya'la informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakkar narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Abi Nur narrated to us from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, concerning ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: [the companions] — every man with every people who used to do his deeds."[98] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/88.]]

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Khalid al-Wahbi narrated to us, saying: Isma'il narrated to us from Simak ibn Harb, that he heard al-Nu'man ibn Bashir say: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾ means: the wicked with the wicked, and the righteous with the righteous. Ibn Abbas said: this is until people become "three classes" (azwaj thalatha). Al-Hasan and Qatada said: each person is joined to his group, Jews with Jews and Christians with Christians. Rabi' ibn Khaytham: a person will be gathered with the companion of his deeds. Muqatil: the souls of the believers are paired with the dark-eyed houris (al-hur al-ʿin), and the souls of the disbelievers with the devils. Its parallel is His words: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾ [[Surat al-Saffat: 22.]]. It was also said: souls are paired with their deeds.

Muhammad ibn Hamdun informed us, saying: Makki informed us, saying: Hamad ibn al-Azhar narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us from his father, from Ikrima, concerning His words, glorified is He: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: the spirits are paired with the bodies.

﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾: the female infant who was killed and buried alive. She was named so because earth is thrown upon her, so it burdens her (yuʾudduhā), that is, weighs her down until she dies. They said: a man of the Arabs, when a daughter was born to him, if he wished to keep her, he would dress her in a garment of wool or hair, and she would herd the camels and sheep in the desert; and if he wished to kill her, he would leave her until she reached six years of age. Then her father would say to her mother: "Perfume her and adorn her, so I may take her to her in-laws," and he had dug a pit for her in the desert. When he brought her to the pit, he would say to her: "Look at this pit," and push her from behind into it, and he would not cast dirt over her head until the pit was level with the ground. This is His words, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿Shall he keep it in humiliation, or bury it in the dust?﴾ [[Surat al-Nahl: 59.]]. Ibn Abbas said: in the Jahiliyya, when a woman became pregnant and the time of her delivery came, she would dig a pit and give birth at the edge of the pit. If she bore a girl, she threw her into the pit; and if she bore a boy, she kept him. Some tribes of the Arabs did this, and about it one of them said:

"I named her, when she was born, 'she will die' / and the grave is a bound in-law I have thrown in."
[[al-Sihah: 1/249.]]

Qatada said: the people of Jahiliyya would kill one of their daughters and feed their dog; Allah reproached them for that and threatened them.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan narrated to us that: al-Furati narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mahdi al-Abbali and Yahya ibn Musa narrated to us, both saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Isra'il ibn Yunus informed us from Simak ibn Harb, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, say concerning the words of Allah, glorified is He:

﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾: Qays ibn Asim al-Tamimi came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I buried eight daughters in the Jahiliyya." He said: "Free a slave for each one of them." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a owner of camels." He said: "Then sacrifice a camel for each of them, if you wish" [99] [[Kanz al-Ummal: 2/546.]].

﴿Asked for what sin she was killed﴾. The common reading is in the passive form in both verbs, and it has two aspects. One: she is asked, and it is said to her: "For what sin were you killed?" and "For what immorality were you killed?" as one says: "Abd Allah said: he is going," and "I am going"; and "Abd Allah said: for what sin was he struck?" and "for what sin was he struck?" Both are permissible and valid. The other: she is asked about by those who buried her, as if you had said: they were asked, and it was said: "Where are your children, and for what sin did you kill them?"

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Muqri informed us, saying: al-Baghawi informed us in Baghdad, saying: Ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us, saying: Ziyad ibn Ayyub Daluyah narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us from a man whom they mention as Harun. Ziyad said: I did not hear it from him myself; from Hashim, from Jabir ibn Zayd, that he used to recite: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked for what sin she was killed﴾; and similarly recited Abu al-Duha and Muslim ibn Subayh.

﴿And when the pages are spread open﴾. The people of Madina, Syria and Basra, except Abu Amr, recited it with light emphasis, and others with the doubled letter, in accordance with His words: ﴿Pages spread open﴾ [[Surat al-Muddathir: 52.]].

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Harun narrated to us, saying: al-Yasiri narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us from Abd al-Hamid ibn Sulayman, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Musa narrated to us from Ata' ibn Bashshar, from Umm Salama, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection naked and barefoot." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about the women?" He said: "People will be occupied, O Umm Salama." She said: "And what will occupy them?" He said: "The spreading of the pages, in which are the weights of atoms and the weights of mustard seeds" [100] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/234.]].

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 81, verses 1–10:

Makkiyya (Meccan), and it has twenty-nine verses, one hundred and four words, and five hundred and thirty letters.

Al-Shaykh al-Imam Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Sahl al-Masarkhi narrated to us by dictation, saying: Abu al-Wafa al-Mu'ammil ibn Isa al-Masarkhi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Qass narrated to us, saying: I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd al-Sana'i say:

I heard Ibn Umar say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever would like to look at the Day of Judgement, let him recite: ﴿When the sun is wound up﴾" [96] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/27; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/226.]].

And Sa'id ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Mutar informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Shurayk narrated to us, saying:

Ahmad ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Salam ibn Sulaym narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir narrated to us from Zayd, from Muslim, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites ﴿When the sun is wound up﴾, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, will protect him from being disgraced when his record is spread open" [97] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/273.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿When the sun is wound up﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn Abbas: it grows dark. Atiyya from him: it departs. Mujahid: it is annihilated. Qatada: its light is gone. Sa'id ibn Jubayr: it is wrapped up (ʿuwwirat), and in Persian kawirikard. Abu Salih: it is turned upside down; and from him also: it is cast down. It is said: "He struck him and kawwarahu," meaning he threw him down. Rabi' ibn Haytham: it is hurled. The basic meaning of takawwur in the speech of the Arabs is gathering one part of a thing onto another, like the winding of a turban (taklwir al-ʿimama), which is wrapping it around the head, and the winding of a bundle (kārah) of plants, which is gathering some of it onto the rest and wrapping it. So the meaning of His words ﴿When the sun is wound up﴾ is: its parts are gathered one onto another, then it is wrapped and thrown, and when this is done to it, its light departs. Its proof and parallel is His words, glorified is He: ﴿And the sun and the moon are joined together﴾ [[Surat al-Qiyama: 9.]].

﴿And when the stars fall, scattering﴾, meaning: they scatter from the sky and fall to the earth. It is said: "inkadara al-tair" means the bird fell from its nest.

Al-Ajjaj said:
"He saw the ḍarbān (a wild beast) in the open and swooped (fa-inkadar)."
[[That is, fa-inṣabb (swooped down); it is in Lisan al-Arab: 4/518.]]

And "inkadara al-qawm" means the people came in successive groups until they swooped down upon them. Dhu al-Rumma said:
"So his wild flank turned aside, and they swooped down, / pursuing without slackening, the hunter and the hunted."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 1/560.]]

Ibn Abbas: it changed.

﴿And when the mountains are set in motion﴾, from the surface of the earth, so they become scattered dust. ﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾: al-ʿishar are the pregnant she-camels in whom ten months of pregnancy have passed; the singular is ʿushara, and this remains their name until they give birth at the completion of a year, and they are at their most precious and valued to their people. ʿUṭṭilat means: left free and neglected; their owners abandoned them, and they were [....] [[Illegible in the manuscript.]] for their tails, so they were not ridden nor milked, and there was no property in the world more beloved to them than these, but they were occupied with other things that distracted them from them.

﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾.

Abd al-Khaliq informed us, saying: Ibn Habib informed us, saying: Abu al-Abbas al-Barti narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us from his father, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾, who said: Their gathering is their death. Ibn Abbas also said: the gathering of everything is death, except the jinn and mankind, for they will be made to stand at the Day of Resurrection. Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾ means: they were mixed together. Qatada: they were assembled. It was also said: they were resurrected so that Allah may judge between them.

﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. The people of Makka and Basra recited it with light emphasis (sukkirat), and others with the doubled letter (sayyirat). They differed about its meaning. Ibn Zayd, Shamir ibn Atiyya, Sufyan and Wahb said: they were kindled and became fire.

That is His words, glorified is He: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. He said: they were mixed. ﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾, he said: He neglected them. ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾, he said: the jinn said to mankind: "We will bring you the news; go to the sea," and behold, it is fire blazing. He said: while they are in that state, the earth splits open in one crack, down to the seventh earth and up to the highest seventh heaven. He said: while they are in that state, a wind comes upon them and causes them to die.

﴿And when the souls are paired﴾.

Al-Hasan informed us, saying: al-Sanni informed us, saying: Abu Ya'la informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakkar narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Abi Nur narrated to us from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, concerning ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: [the companions] — every man with every people who used to do his deeds."[98] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/88.]]

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Khalid al-Wahbi narrated to us, saying: Isma'il narrated to us from Simak ibn Harb, that he heard al-Nu'man ibn Bashir say: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾ means: the wicked with the wicked, and the righteous with the righteous. Ibn Abbas said: this is until people become "three classes" (azwaj thalatha). Al-Hasan and Qatada said: each person is joined to his group, Jews with Jews and Christians with Christians. Rabi' ibn Khaytham: a person will be gathered with the companion of his deeds. Muqatil: the souls of the believers are paired with the dark-eyed houris (al-hur al-ʿin), and the souls of the disbelievers with the devils. Its parallel is His words: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾ [[Surat al-Saffat: 22.]]. It was also said: souls are paired with their deeds.

Muhammad ibn Hamdun informed us, saying: Makki informed us, saying: Hamad ibn al-Azhar narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us from his father, from Ikrima, concerning His words, glorified is He: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: the spirits are paired with the bodies.

﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾: the female infant who was killed and buried alive. She was named so because earth is thrown upon her, so it burdens her (yuʾudduhā), that is, weighs her down until she dies. They said: a man of the Arabs, when a daughter was born to him, if he wished to keep her, he would dress her in a garment of wool or hair, and she would herd the camels and sheep in the desert; and if he wished to kill her, he would leave her until she reached six years of age. When he brought her to the pit, he would say to her: "Look at this pit," and push her from behind into it, and he would not cast dirt over her head until the pit was level with the ground. This is His words, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿Shall he keep it in humiliation, or bury it in the dust?﴾ [[Surat al-Nahl: 59.]]. Ibn Abbas said: in the Jahiliyya, when a woman became pregnant and the time of her delivery came, she would dig a pit and give birth at the edge of the pit. If she bore a girl, she threw her into the pit; and if she bore a boy, she kept him. Some tribes of the Arabs did this, and about it one of them said:

"I named her, when she was born, 'she will die' / and the grave is a bound in-law I have thrown in."
[[al-Sihah: 1/249.]]

Qatada said: the people of Jahiliyya would kill one of their daughters and feed their dog; Allah reproached them for that and threatened them.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan narrated to us that: al-Furati narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mahdi al-Abbali and Yahya ibn Musa narrated to us, both saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Isra'il ibn Yunus informed us from Simak ibn Harb, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, say concerning the words of Allah, glorified is He:

﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾: Qays ibn Asim al-Tamimi came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I buried eight daughters in the Jahiliyya." He said: "Free a slave for each one of them." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a owner of camels." He said: "Then sacrifice a camel for each of them, if you wish" [99] [[Kanz al-Ummal: 2/546.]].

﴿Asked for what sin she was killed﴾. The common reading is in the passive form in both verbs, and it has two aspects. One: she is asked, and it is said to her: "For what sin were you killed?" and "For what immorality were you killed?" as one says: "Abd Allah said: he is going," and "I am going"; and "Abd Allah said: for what sin was he struck?" and "for what sin was he struck?" Both are permissible and valid. The other: she is asked about by those who buried her, as if you had said: they were asked, and it was said: "Where are your children, and for what sin did you kill them?"

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Muqri informed us, saying: al-Baghawi informed us in Baghdad, saying: Ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us, saying: Ziyad ibn Ayyub Daluyah narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us from a man whom they mention as Harun. Ziyad said: I did not hear it from him myself; from Hashim, from Jabir ibn Zayd, that he used to recite: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked for what sin she was killed﴾; and similarly recited Abu al-Duha and Muslim ibn Subayh.

﴿And when the pages are spread open﴾. The people of Madina, Syria and Basra, except Abu Amr, recited it with light emphasis, and others with the doubled letter, in accordance with His words: ﴿Pages spread open﴾ [[Surat al-Muddathir: 52.]].

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Harun narrated to us, saying: al-Yasiri narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us from Abd al-Hamid ibn Sulayman, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Musa narrated to us from Ata' ibn Bashshar, from Umm Salama, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection naked and barefoot." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about the women?" He said: "People will be occupied, O Umm Salama." She said: "And what will occupy them?" He said: "The spreading of the pages, in which are the weights of atoms and the weights of mustard seeds" [100] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/234.]].

﴿And when the sky is stripped away﴾: that is, it is acted upon, pulled out and drawn away from its places, and then rolled up. In the reading of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud), it is *qashatat* with a *qaf*. Both are dialectal variants. In Arabic speech, the *qaf* and the *kaf* alternate in their articulation, as in *al-kafur* and *al-qafur*, and *qaff* and *kaff*.

﴿And when the Hellfire is set ablaze﴾: The people of Medina read *su''irat* with the doubled *'ayn* (intensive form), and the others read *su'irat* without doubling. Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred the latter, because the meaning is one. The readings differed between Ibn 'Asim and Ibn 'Amir. The meaning is: it was kindled. Qatadah said: "The wrath of God and the sins of the children of Adam kindle it."

﴿And when Paradise is brought near﴾: it is brought near to its people. A parallel is His saying: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous﴾ [[Surah al-Shu'ara': 90.]]. ﴿Then every soul will know what it has presented﴾, of good or evil. This is the answer to His saying ﴿When the sun is wound up﴾ and what follows, as one says: "When Zayd stood up, 'Amr sat down."

Ibn 'Abbas, on His saying ﴿When the sun is wound up﴾ up to ﴿every soul will know﴾, said: there are twelve characteristics, six in this world and six in the Hereafter.

﴿So I swear by the receding stars, the ones that run and hide﴾. Some people said: they are the five planets, the wandering stars. They recede in their courses, turning back behind, and they hide (*yaknus*) at the time of their disappearance, which is their setting, as gazelles hide in their lairs. Qatadah said: they are the stars that appear at night and are hidden by day, so they are not seen.

The evidence for this interpretation is what Shu'bah narrated from Simak, from Khalid ibn 'Ar'arah, that a man of Murad said to 'Ali: "What are *al-khunnas al-jawari al-kunnas*?" He said: "They are the stars that recede by day so they are not seen, and that hide by night, returning to their courses. They are Bahram, Zuhal, 'Utarid, Zuhrah, and Mushtari (Jupiter)."

Ibn Zayd said: the meaning of *khunnas* is that they recede, that is, they fall back from their risings. Each year they fall behind by an amount relative to the earlier rising. They recede from it. *Yaknusna* means they hide by day, so they are not seen.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn al-Nawwab told us, saying: Radwan ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar told us, saying: Abu Ma'unah told us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Abdullah, concerning His saying ﴿al-jawari al-kunnas﴾: they are wild cattle. Ibrahim and Jabir ibn Zayd held this view. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they are gazelles, which is also the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

The root of *khunnas* is returning backward. *Kunus* means that it retreats to its *makanis*, which are the places where wild animals take shelter. Al-A'sha said:

"When we reached the tribe, it stretched its neck and receded,
as the wild cows stretch their necks beneath the shelters."

They are also called *kanais*. Tarafah ibn al-'Abd said:

"As if my two shelters were a stray's two hiding places,
and her two hooves beneath the firm ground."

Aws ibn Hajar said:

"Have you not seen that God sent down His cloud,
and the gazelles in their shelters were roused and scattered?"

﴿And by the night when it turns away﴾: al-Hasan said: it approaches with its darkness. Others said: it withdraws. The Arabs say: *'asa'sa al-layl* and *sa'sa'a* when it turns away and little of it remains. 'Alqamah ibn Qurt said:

"Until, when the dawn breathed upon it
and the night withdrew from it and retreated."

Ru'bah said:

"O Hind, how quickly you have become (lit. 'grown') a worn-out one,
after you were a young, slender youth."

﴿And by the dawn when it breathes﴾: it approaches and shines, and its beginning appears. It was also said: it extends and rises.

﴿Indeed, it (the Qur'an) is the word of a noble messenger﴾, that is, Gabriel (peace be upon him). ﴿Possessed of power, with rank before the Owner of the Throne, obeyed there and trustworthy﴾: he is there in the heaven, obeyed by the angels, and trustworthy with the revelation. ﴿And your companion is not a madman﴾, meaning Muhammad. ﴿And he had certainly seen him﴾, meaning Gabriel in his true form, ﴿on the clear horizon﴾. It is the highest horizon on the side of the east from which the day comes. This was said by Mujahid and Qatadah.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Makhlad told us, saying: Ibn 'Alawayh told us, saying: Isma'il told us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr told us, saying: Ibn Juraij told us, from 'Ikrimah, and Muqatil, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said:

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to Gabriel: "I love to see you in your form in which you are in the heaven." He said: "You will not be able to bear it." He said: "Yes." He said: "Where do you wish me to appear to you?" He said: "In al-Abtah." He said: "It cannot contain me." He said: "In Mina." He said: "It cannot contain me." He said: "In 'Arafat." He said: "That is more fitting to contain me." So he made an appointment with him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) went out at the appointed time, and behold, Gabriel (peace be upon him) came from the mountains of 'Arafat, with his great body and his bulk filling what is between the east and the west, his head in the heaven and his feet on the earth. When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw him, he fell unconscious. Gabriel then changed into his form and embraced him to his breast, saying: "O Muhammad, do not fear. How would it be if you saw Israfil, whose head is beneath the Throne and whose feet are in the seventh heavens? The Throne itself rests upon his shoulder, and he sometimes shrinks out of fear of God, the Mighty and Majestic, until he becomes like a *wadi* (a small bird, the sparrow), so that the Throne of your Lord is borne only by his bones."

Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred the latter, because the meaning is one. The readings differed between Ibn 'Asim and Ibn 'Amir. The meaning is: it was kindled. Qatadah said: "The wrath of God and the sins of the children of Adam kindle it."

﴿And when Paradise is brought near﴾: it is brought near to its people. A parallel is His saying: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous﴾ [[Surah al-Shu'ara': 90.]]. ﴿Then every soul will know what it has presented﴾, of good or evil. This is the answer to His saying ﴿When the sun is wound up﴾ and what follows, as one says: "When Zayd stood up, 'Amr sat down."

Ibn 'Abbas, on His saying ﴿When the sun is wound up﴾ up to ﴿every soul will know﴾, said: there are twelve characteristics, six in this world and six in the Hereafter.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn al-Nawwab told us, saying: Radwan ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar told us, saying: Abu Ma'unah told us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Abdullah, concerning His saying ﴿al-jawari al-kunnas﴾: they are wild cattle. Ibrahim and Jabir ibn Zayd held this view. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they are gazelles, which is also the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

The root of *khunnas* is returning backward. *Kunus* means that it retreats to its *makanis*, which are the places where wild animals take shelter. Al-A'sha said:

"When we reached the tribe, it stretched its neck and receded,
as the wild cows stretch their necks beneath the shelters."

They are also called *kanais*. Tarafah ibn al-'Abd said:

"As if my two shelters were a stray's two hiding places,
and her two hooves beneath the firm ground."

Aws ibn Hajar said:

"Have you not seen that God sent down His cloud,
and the gazelles in their shelters were roused and scattered?"

﴿And by the night when it turns away﴾: al-Hasan said: it approaches with its darkness. Others said: it withdraws. The Arabs say: *'asa'sa al-layl* and *sa'sa'a* when it turns away and little of it remains. 'Alqamah ibn Qurt said:

"Until, when the dawn breathed upon it
and the night withdrew from it and retreated."

Ru'bah said:

"O Hind, how quickly you have become (lit. 'grown') a worn-out one,
after you were a young, slender youth."

It is the highest horizon on the side of the east from which the day comes. This was said by Mujahid and Qatadah.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Makhlad told us, saying: Ibn 'Alawayh told us, saying: Isma'il told us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr told us, saying: Ibn Juraij told us, from 'Ikrimah, and Muqatil, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said:

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to Gabriel: "I love to see you in your form in which you are in the heaven." He said: "You will not be able to bear it." He said: "Yes." He said: "Where do you wish me to appear to you?" He said: "In al-Abtah." He said: "It cannot contain me." He said: "In Mina." He said: "It cannot contain me." He said: "In 'Arafat." He said: "That is more fitting to contain me." So he made an appointment with him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) went out at the appointed time, and behold, Gabriel (peace be upon him) came from the mountains of 'Arafat, with his great body and his bulk filling what is between the east and the west, his head in the heaven and his feet on the earth. When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw him, he fell unconscious. Gabriel then changed into his form and embraced him to his breast, saying: "O Muhammad, do not fear. How would it be if you saw Israfil, whose head is beneath the Throne and whose feet are in the seventh heavens? The Throne itself rests upon his shoulder, and he sometimes shrinks out of fear of God, the Mighty and Majestic, until he becomes like a *wadi* (a small bird, the sparrow), so that the Throne of your Lord is borne only by his bones."

The rest read it with the *za'* (ẓ). It is the same in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud and his *mushaf*. Al-Junayd said: the meaning of this verse is linked with another verse, namely His saying, glorified and exalted: ﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasuries﴾ [[Surah al-Hijr: 21.]], so where could they go?

﴿It is not but a reminder to the worlds, for whoever among you wills to be upright﴾, that is, to follow the truth, act by it, and remain steadfast upon it. Then He said: ﴿And you do not will except that God wills, the Lord of the worlds﴾.

Abu Bakr ibn 'Abdus, the one who purifies, informed us, saying: Abu Hamid ibn Hilal al-Bazzaz told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami told us, saying: Abu Mushir told us, saying: Sa'id told me, from Sulayman ibn Musa, who said: When God, glorified and exalted, revealed ﴿for whoever among you wills to be upright﴾, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham said: "That is up to us. If we wish, we will be upright, and if we wish, we will not be upright." So God revealed ﴿And you do not will except that God wills, the Lord of the worlds﴾.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah told us, saying: al-Farmi [[He is Abu 'Ali al-Farmi, the nisba of al-Farr, a city on the coast of Egypt (Mu'jam al-Buldan).]] told us, saying: Malik ibn Sulayman told me, saying: Baqiyyah told us, from 'Umar ibn Muhammad, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: When God, glorified and exalted, revealed to His Messenger ﴿for whoever among you wills to be upright﴾, they said: "The matter is up to us. If we wish, we will be upright, and if we wish, we will not be upright." So God, glorified and exalted, revealed: ﴿And you do not will except that God wills, the Lord of the worlds﴾.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Mihran told us, saying: Abu Muslim al-Kanji told us, saying: Ja'far ibn Jubayr ibn Farqad told us, saying: I heard a man ask al-Hasan about the saying of God, glorified and exalted: ﴿And you do not will except that God wills, the Lord of the worlds﴾. Al-Hasan said: "By God, the Arabs did not will Islam until God willed it for them."

al-Hasan informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn told us, saying: 'Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Bisṭam told us, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Hajjaj al-Shami told us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, saying: Abu Sinan told us, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: The books that God, glorified and exalted, sent down upon the prophets are ninety-some books. I read eighty-some of them and found in them: "Whoever ascribes to himself any share of will has disbelieved."

Al-Wasiti said: He has made you incapable in all your attributes, so you do not will except His will, and you do not act except by His power, and you do not obey except by His grace, and you do not disobey except by His abandonment of you. Then what remains for you, and what do you boast of in your deeds, when none of your deeds is yours?

﴿And when the sky is stripped away﴾: that is, it is acted upon, pulled out and drawn away from its places, and then rolled up. In the reading of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud), it is *qashatat* with a *qaf*. Both are dialectal variants. In Arabic speech, the *qaf* and the *kaf* alternate in their articulation, as in *al-kafur* and *al-qafur*, and *qaff* and *kaff*.

﴿And when the Hellfire is set ablaze﴾: The people of Medina read *su''irat* with the doubled *'ayn* (intensive form), and the others read *su'irat* without doubling. Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred the latter, because the meaning is one. The readings differed between Ibn 'Asim and Ibn 'Amir. The meaning is: it was kindled. Qatadah said: "The wrath of God and the sins of the children of Adam kindle it."

﴿And when Paradise is brought near﴾: it is brought near to its people. A parallel is His saying: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous﴾ [[Surah al-Shu'ara': 90.]]. ﴿Then every soul will know what it has presented﴾, of good or evil. This is the answer to His saying ﴿When the sun is wound up﴾ and what follows, as one says: "When Zayd stood up, 'Amr sat down."

Ibn 'Abbas, on His saying ﴿When the sun is wound up﴾ up to ﴿every soul will know﴾, said: there are twelve characteristics, six in this world and six in the Hereafter.

﴿So I swear by the receding stars, the ones that run and hide﴾. Some people said: they are the five planets, the wandering stars. They recede in their courses, turning back behind, and they hide (*yaknus*) at the time of their disappearance, which is their setting, as gazelles hide in their lairs. Qatadah said: they are the stars that appear at night and are hidden by day, so they are not seen.

The evidence for this interpretation is what Shu'bah narrated from Simak, from Khalid ibn 'Ar'arah, that a man of Murad said to 'Ali: "What are *al-khunnas al-jawari al-kunnas*?" He said: "They are the stars that recede by day so they are not seen, and that hide by night, returning to their courses. They are Bahram, Zuhal, 'Utarid, Zuhrah, and Mushtari (Jupiter)."

Ibn Zayd said: the meaning of *khunnas* is that they recede, that is, they fall back from their risings. Each year they fall behind by an amount relative to the earlier rising. They recede from it. *Yaknusna* means they hide by day, so they are not seen.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn al-Nawwab told us, saying: Radwan ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar told us, saying: Abu Ma'unah told us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Abdullah, concerning His saying ﴿al-jawari al-kunnas﴾: they are wild cattle. Ibrahim and Jabir ibn Zayd held this view. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they are gazelles, which is also the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

The root of *khunnas* is returning backward. *Kunus* means that it retreats to its *makanis*, which are the places where wild animals take shelter. Al-A'sha said:

"When we reached the tribe, it stretched its neck and receded,
as the wild cows stretch their necks beneath the shelters."

They are also called *kanais*. Tarafah ibn al-'Abd said:

"As if my two shelters were a stray's two hiding places,
and her two hooves beneath the firm ground."

Aws ibn Hajar said:

"Have you not seen that God sent down His cloud,
and the gazelles in their shelters were roused and scattered?"

﴿And by the night when it turns away﴾: al-Hasan said: it approaches with its darkness. Others said: it withdraws. The Arabs say: *'asa'sa al-layl* and *sa'sa'a* when it turns away and little of it remains. 'Alqamah ibn Qurt said:

"Until, when the dawn breathed upon it
and the night withdrew from it and retreated."

Ru'bah said:

"O Hind, how quickly you have become (lit. 'grown') a worn-out one,
after you were a young, slender youth."

﴿And by the dawn when it breathes﴾: it approaches and shines, and its beginning appears. It was also said: it extends and rises.

﴿Indeed, it (the Qur'an) is the word of a noble messenger﴾, that is, Gabriel (peace be upon him). ﴿Possessed of power, with rank before the Owner of the Throne, obeyed there and trustworthy﴾: he is there in the heaven, obeyed by the angels, and trustworthy with the revelation. ﴿And your companion is not a madman﴾, meaning Muhammad. ﴿And he had certainly seen him﴾, meaning Gabriel in his true form, ﴿on the clear horizon﴾. It is the highest horizon on the side of the east from which the day comes. This was said by Mujahid and Qatadah.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Makhlad told us, saying: Ibn 'Alawayh told us, saying: Isma'il told us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr told us, saying: Ibn Juraij told us, from 'Ikrimah, and Muqatil, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said:

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to Gabriel: "I love to see you in your form in which you are in the heaven." He said: "You will not be able to bear it." He said: "Yes." He said: "Where do you wish me to appear to you?" He said: "In al-Abtah." He said: "It cannot contain me." He said: "In Mina." He said: "It cannot contain me." He said: "In 'Arafat." He said: "That is more fitting to contain me." So he made an appointment with him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) went out at the appointed time, and behold, Gabriel (peace be upon him) came from the mountains of 'Arafat, with his great body and his bulk filling what is between the east and the west, his head in the heaven and his feet on the earth. When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw him, he fell unconscious. Gabriel then changed into his form and embraced him to his breast, saying: "O Muhammad, do not fear. How would it be if you saw Israfil, whose head is beneath the Throne and whose feet are in the seventh heavens? The Throne itself rests upon his shoulder, and he sometimes shrinks out of fear of God, the Mighty and Majestic, until he becomes like a *wadi* (a small bird, the sparrow), so that the Throne of your Lord is borne only by his bones."

﴿And he is not one who withholds﴾: that is, Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Concerning the unseen﴾: that is, the revelation, the news of heaven, and what he was made aware of from the knowledge of the unseen. ﴿Stingy (*bi-dhanin*)﴾: Zayd ibn Thabit, al-Hasan, Ibn 'Amr, al-Ashhab, 'Asim, al-A'mash, Hamzah, and the people of Medina and Syria read it with the *dad* (ḍ). It is the same in the codex of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and it is the reading of Ibn 'Abbas as transmitted by Mujahid, and Abu Hatim preferred it. Its meaning is "he is stingy." He says: the knowledge of the unseen comes to him, and it is inscribed in it, so he does not withhold it from you, but teaches you and informs you of it. The Arabs say: *danantu bi-al-shay'* (with the *nun* vowelled with a kasra), *adinnu bihi dannan wa-dannanatan*, so *fa-ana dhanin*, meaning stingy. The poet said:

"I give generously from my inherited wealth, and I am
not withholding your secret from one who asks me."

The rest read it with the *za'* (ẓ). It is the same in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud and his *mushaf*. This is the reading of 'Abdullah, 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, Abu 'Abd al-Sulami, and the transmission of Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas. Its meaning is that he accuses them, as one says: "So-and-so is suspected of wealth and accused of wealth," that is, he is accused of it. *Al-zunnah* means accusation. The poet said:

"By the Book of God, I did not abandon him out of hatred,
but the accused (*al-zanin*) is (still) accused."

Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading and said: they did not accuse him of stinginess, so that it would need to be denied of him. Rather, they denied him and accused him. Moreover, most of Arabic speech says "he is not accused of such-and-such" and does not say "he is not upon such-and-such"; they say "you are not accused of such-and-such." It was said that *zanin* means weak, which was reported by al-Farra' and al-Mubarrad. One says *rajul zanin*, that is, weak, and *bi'r dannun* when its water is weak. Al-A'sha said:

"What has made the weak well (*al-jadd al-zanun*) that turned away from the rushing rain
like the Euphrates when it overflows and casts up the Bawsi (a kind of ship) and the swimmer?"

﴿And it is not the word of an accursed devil﴾, meaning the Qur'an. ﴿So where are you going?﴾, meaning: where do you turn away from this Qur'an, in which is healing and clarity? Al-Kisa'i said: I heard the Arabs say: *inṭalaqa bihi al-ghawr* (he went off with it to the lowland). Al-Farra' related from the Arabs: *dhahabat al-Sham* (I went to Syria), *kharajtu al-'Iraq* (I went out to Iraq), *inṭalaqtu al-suq* (I went off to the market), meaning [...] [Blank in the manuscript.] He said: we heard these three words, and one of the Banu 'Uqayl recited to me:

"Hanifah shouts at us when they see us,
and to what land do you go with the shouting?"

He means: to which land do you go?
